flashcard_questions.q: Which line does the sleepwalking Lady Macbeth cry as she scrubs her hands?
Which Act Five line reverses her earlier claim that water would clean them?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘All the perfumes of Arabia will not sweeten this little hand.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which form does Shakespeare give Lady Macbeth’s Act Five speech, rather than verse?
What does that switch from verse signal about Lady Macbeth?
flashcard_questions.a: A loss of control and status as her mind breaks down.

flashcard_questions.q: Which murder does Lady Macbeth recall with ‘The Thane of Fife had a wife’?
What does Lady Macbeth now insist on having beside her at all times?
Which earlier invocation shows Lady Macbeth once welcoming darkness?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Come, thick night, and pall thee in the dunnest smoke of hell.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which line of the Doctor’s ties her madness to the broken natural order?
What is an ironic reversal in a play?
flashcard_questions.a: A contrast between what a character once believed and what they now experience.

flashcard_questions.q: Which prophecy does Macbeth cling to in Act Five, Scene Three?
flashcard_questions.a: That he cannot fear until Birnam Wood moves to Dunsinane.

flashcard_questions.q: Which colour do all Macbeth’s insults to his servants share?
Which name does Macbeth use for his wife by Act Five?
How does Macbeth react to the news that his wife is dead?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘She should have died hereafter’ — detached, with no grief.

flashcard_questions.q: What is nihilism as a philosophy?
flashcard_questions.a: The belief that life is meaningless and has no purpose or inherent value.

flashcard_questions.q: Which phrase ends the ‘tomorrow’ speech and sums up Macbeth’s nihilism?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Full of sound and fury, signifying nothing.’

notes: 15 cards: 7 quotation-recall fronts, 3 quotation-to-effect (the prose shift, the servant insults, Macbeth’s flat reaction), 2 term-to-definition (ironic reversal, nihilism), 1 form card (prose not verse), 1 symbol-to-meaning (light kept continually), 1 plot fact (the Birnam Wood prophecy). ‘Great Chain of Being’ and ‘symbol’ dropped as glossary restatements; the existing ‘brief candle’ card was replaced by the closing phrase of the same speech to avoid repeating it. All quotations verbatim from the lesson content.
